title: Elasticity rulebook and safety wrapping for dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Design and prototype a policy "rulebook" and a safety-wrapping layer for Redwood Dedicated autoscaling that composes multiple target metrics (latency percentiles, token throughput, slot occupancy, queue length, warm-start rate) into deterministic scaling intents, and applies hard fences and soft throttles to prevent disruptive oscillations and cost blowouts.

Why: Existing policies address single-metric targets or percentile-based thresholds. Production fleets need a reproducible, auditable policy that can: (1) honor committed throughput contracts, (2) prioritize tenant SLAs, (3) gracefully degrade with fallback model-variants, and (4) enforce strict safety limits (max GPUs, burst budgets) across heterogeneous instance types.

Key concepts and design decisions so far: 
- Metric composition: we will synthesize a single "scaling demand score" by normalized aggregation of P95 latency headroom, recent sustained token-ps (windowed 1m/5m), queue growth rate, and warm-start fraction. Normalization is percentile-based with tunable weights per project/tenant.
- Targeting semantics: support two simultaneous targets — "contracted throughput" (hard target expressed in tokens/s or slots) and "latency headroom" (soft target expressed as target p95). Contracted throughput is always satisfied up to capacity and takes precedence during contention.
- Scaling algorithms: primary actor is a constrained stepper with proportional+derivative correction (PD-stepper) for stable reaction to demand changes; secondary actor runs a periodic packer that performs discrete slot allocation (greedy knapsack variant) to convert desired capacity into concrete fleet changes across heterogeneous SKUs.
- Safety wrapping: implement a multi-layer safety wrapper that enforces (a) absolute hard caps per-tenant and global max-GPUs, (b) burst budget accounting with exponential decay, (c) minimum stabilization windows (configurable), and (d) KV-affinity-aware rollback windows to avoid evicting hot caches.
- Predictive warm-up: integrate a short predictive warm-up phase where the autoscaler requests a small extra buffer to pre-warm model caches when warm-start fraction drops below threshold. This is budgeted against the tenant's burst credit.
- Observability & audit: every scaling decision must emit a deterministic decision record (inputs, score breakdown, chosen action, safety overrides) to the console audit log for replay and postmortem.

Trade-offs discussed: 
- Aggressiveness vs cost: PD-stepper configuration favors stability; aggressive P-only controllers reduce latency faster but cause cost spikes. We're defaulting to conservative PD gains with an emergency fast-path that can only be triggered by on-call override or detected global SLA violations.
- Complexity vs transparency: packer adds scheduling realism for heterogeneous SKUs, but makes step-to-action mapping less trivial. Decision record will include packer reasoning to preserve transparency.
- Warm-up budget fairness: allocating pre-warm slots reduces immediate availability for others; we propose charging burst budgets and denying warm-up when close to budget exhaustion.

Proposed config surface for users/tenant teams: 
- target_weights: list (p95_latency, sustained_tokens, queue_growth, warm_fraction) as CSV string of floats 
- contracted_throughput: string (tokens/s or slots)
- max_gpu_cap: string (integer)
- burst_budget_tokens: string (integer)
- stabilization_window_secs: string
- packer_preference: string (cost|latency|balanced)
- kv_affinity_loss_tolerance: string (percentage)

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Decision simulation harness reproduces expected stepper output on 10 synthetic workload traces (spikes, diurnal, gradual ramp, noisy) with documented score breakdowns.
2) Safety wrapper prevents any scaling action that would exceed max_gpu_cap or burst budget in simulated tests.
3) Packaged telemetry events allow reconstructing decisions end-to-end in the Console audit log.
4) PR with design doc + prototype in feature branch: runtime/autoscaler/elastbook with unit tests and integration tests against the simulator.

Artifacts & links: 
- Design doc (living): https://company-confluence.internal/redwood/dedicated/autoscale-rulebook (draft)
- Simulator job and traces: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SimulatorTraces (internal)
- Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1429 (WIP)

Open questions: 
- Do we allow per-tenant override of PD gains in self-serve or restrict to platform SRE? (PM prefers limited self-serve for power users)
- How should contracted throughput map to slot vs tokens/s for composite models (mixtures of short and long generation queries)?
- What is the acceptable cold-start budget window that customers will accept before we count a warmup as a denial-of-service?

- Finalize decision record schema with Console team (Ava) — target 2026-03-12 (in review).
- Spike PR to add packer algorithm and unit tests (Esteban) — target 2026-03-24.
